comments.body:
SCOPING DECISION, RECORDED SO IT CAN BE OVERRULED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. This bug is NOT
being made a child of epic e369-a449-4773-48fb, and therefore does not block that epic's closure.

THE ARGUMENT FOR PUTTING IT IN e369: the operator's standing precedent on that epic is that
PRE-EXISTING DEFECTS IN SHARED PATHS THAT DC SHIPS ARE IN SCOPE — that is why 387d and 7c26 were
pulled in despite being neither new nor DC-specific. This defect is in DC's shipped comment path, so
the precedent reaches it.

THE ARGUMENT AGAINST, which is why it is filed as a follow-up:
 1. SEVERITY. The truncation is not silent to the operator — jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148 emits
    a warning — and the hardcoded value is CORRECT for a stock instance. The data-loss window opens
    only where an admin has raised or removed the limit. Contrast 21fc (wrote duplicate issues) or
    deac (lost 92% of an inbound snapshot), which were the defects that earned the precedent.
 2. THE OWNING STORY EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES IT. 79d5's Scope says a limit/behaviour change 'belongs in
    its own bug ticket linked from here — not folded into a test story', and its ACs say the story
    must NOT silently change the limit. Folding this in would violate the plan that was written to
    prevent exactly that.
 3. IT WOULD CONTRADICT THE STATED DONE-CONDITION. The current instruction is that the work is done
    when e369 is closed and every P1 child of 3e73 is closed. Attaching a newly-discovered
    configurability feature to e369 extends that epic on the strength of research rather than of a
    failure, which is how an epic stops converging.

SO THE DEFAULT IS: fix it after e369 and 3e73's P1 children. If the operator prefers the stricter
reading of the precedent, reparent this under e369 and it becomes a blocker — that is a one-command
change (rebar edit 049e-9fac-a821-4ea2 --parent e369-a449-4773-48fb) and nothing here depends on the
current choice.

Also worth stating plainly, because it is the reason this ticket exists at all: the defect was found
by DOCUMENTARY RESEARCH, not by a test and not by the live harness. The harness is one
default-configured 8.17.1 instance, so its jira.text.field.character.limit is 32767 and it can never
exhibit this bug no matter how long it runs. That is the same structural blind spot epic 3e73 was
commissioned to address, showing up once more.

comments.body:
IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE — Gerrit change 1261 ("Make DC comment ceiling configurable"),
Change-Id I597830964f20f266ba0ee92eac775e7645524e61, one commit, branch agent-049e off
origin/main 6cdd4b00d9.

WHAT LANDED (4 files)
 1. src/rebar/_config_schema.py — new key ReconcilerConfig.comment_max_chars: int = 32767,
    plus its coercer in _SECTIONS["reconciler"]: _as_int(minimum=0, maximum=2147483647),
    which is jira.text.field.character.limit's own documented range. IDIOM COPIED: the
    existing DC connection settings on the same dataclass (base_url / allow_insecure /
    ca_bundle / resolved_statuses, story J6) — a defaulted field on ReconcilerConfig plus a
    coercer row; that gives the AUTO-DERIVED canonical env override
    REBAR_RECONCILER_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS for free via _config_sources._canonical_env_name, so no
    entry in _CANONICAL_ENV_NAMES was needed (that table is only for ergonomic renames such as
    reconciler.jira_cli_timeout -> REBAR_JIRA_CLI_TIMEOUT). Precedence therefore follows the
    standard layering CLI > env > project > user > default.
 2. adapters/jira_datacenter/settings.py — new resolve_comment_max_chars(); its docstring is
    the provenance citation required by AC1 (jpm.xml default-value 32767 with the "Description,
    Environment, Comments and Text custom fields / 0 means unlimited" scope, plus
    JRASERVER-28519's 7.0.0 default), and it also records why discovery is dropped. Returns 0
    for a non-positive value, which the truncator treats as unlimited.
 3. adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py — new module-level _truncate_dc_comment_body(body,
    max_chars) (the comment path's OWN rule); _DCSanitizer gained an optional
    comment_max_chars constructor argument plus a lazy+cached comment_max_chars() resolver
    (lazy because _DCSanitizer is built in JiraDataCenterBackend.__init__, which must not
    require a resolvable config; a plain METHOD, not a property, so the py3.11
    runtime_checkable-Protocol hazard documented in settings.py is not reintroduced).
    sanitize_comment and fit_comment BOTH route through the new truncator.
 4. NEW tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_comment_ceiling_049e.py — 6 tests.

AC4, DECOUPLING FROM THE DESCRIPTION FITTER — HOW
 sanitize_comment previously passed truncate=self._codec.fit_outbound and
 max_chars=WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT into the shared jira_family.sanitize_comment, and
 fit_comment WAS self._codec.fit_outbound. Both now call _truncate_dc_comment_body(text,
 self.comment_max_chars()) instead, and WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT is no longer imported by
 backend.py at all. The one thing still shared with rich_text.py is the inert marker STRING
 _WIKI_TRUNCATION_SUFFIX, imported rather than redeclared so a DC reader keeps seeing ONE
 truncation marker and so byte-identity with the description rule at the default ceiling is
 preserved (that identity is what the pre-existing test_dc_backend_characterization
 "fit_comment is the wiki codec fit" and state/test_richtext_port_heldout
 "byte-identical to the vendor rule" assertions pin — they still pass UNCHANGED, so no
 existing assertion was weakened). Sharing a marker string is not the trap; sharing the
 fitter FUNCTION was, because Cloud's description fitter measures ADF-SERIALIZED size.
 Convergence between the send-side and differ-side transforms is now structural (one
 function, one ceiling) and is asserted directly by the new
 test_fit_comment_converges_with_sanitize_comment.

AC3, IS /rest/api/2/application-properties READABLE BY REBAR'S NON-ADMIN PAT? ANSWER: NO —
DISCOVERY IS DROPPED. Recorded honestly, including the limits of the evidence:
 * A LIVE probe against the project's own harness was NOT possible on this host. The harness
   (tests/external/live_jira_dc) is amd64-only and its README records three measured attempts
   in which Jira never became usable within an hour on this project's arm64 workstation; no DC
   instance was running (docker ps checked, nothing on 2990), and standing one up was not a
   viable step. So this determination is DOCUMENTARY, not a 403 captured from our own credential.
 * The documented requirement for the application-properties resource — and specifically for
   the /advanced-settings sub-resource, which is where jira.text.field.character.limit is
   actually exposed (the Atlassian Community answer people are pointed at uses
   /rest/api/latest/application-properties/advanced-settings) — is the "Administer Jira"
   GLOBAL permission. Jira DC's own 8.17.1 REST reference states no permission at all for
   GET /rest/api/2/application-properties, so it is not a counter-source; the permission
   statement is consistent across the v2/v3 platform docs.
 * rebar authenticates as an ordinary user's PAT, so the probe would 403 for exactly the
   population that needs it (an operator who raised the limit is not necessarily a Jira admin,
   and rebar's credential normally is not one). Building a discovery probe on that would add a
   network call that fails closed and teaches the operator nothing.
 * DECISION: proposed remediation step 2 (probe application-properties at connect time and warn
   on disagreement) is DROPPED. Configuration is the whole remedy. This is written into
   resolve_comment_max_chars's docstring so the next reader does not re-open it. If someone
   later gets an admin-credentialed DC instance and wants the warning, that is a NEW ticket
   with a live 200/403 capture as its first acceptance criterion.

RED-FIRST EVIDENCE (test written and run before any src change)
 5 failed, 1 passed. Every failure an AssertionError — no ImportError, no AttributeError, no
 TypeError. Headline message:
   test_raised_ceiling_returns_the_body_whole
   AssertionError: comment was TRUNCATED to 32767 chars under a ceiling configured to 100000:
   rebar applied its compiled-in 32767 instead of the configured
   jira.text.field.character.limit, which is admin-settable on Data Center
 The one test that passed RED is test_unconfigured_default_is_still_the_stock_ceiling, which is
 correct: the default was already right and must not move.
 The RED was driven through the PUBLIC surface (env override + _DCSanitizer().sanitize_comment)
 rather than through the not-yet-existing config key, precisely so the failure was a truncation
 and not an AttributeError.

MUTATION CHECK — two mutations, both VALID (assertion failures, not import/attribute errors)
 MUTATED: resolve_comment_max_chars body replaced with "return 32767" (reverts configurability
   entirely, keeping the symbol so the failure cannot be an ImportError);
   FAILED: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_comment_ceiling_049e.py::test_raised_ceiling_returns_the_body_whole
   with exactly the headline RED message above (AssertionError: comment was TRUNCATED to 32767
   chars under a ceiling configured to 100000 ...), plus test_zero_ceiling_means_unlimited,
   test_lowered_ceiling_is_honored and test_fit_comment_converges_with_sanitize_comment
   (AssertionError: assert 32767 == 4096). 5 failed, 1 passed.
 MUTATED: sanitize_comment's truncate= argument recoupled to self._codec.fit_outbound (the
   description fitter);
   FAILED: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_comment_ceiling_049e.py::test_sanitize_comment_does_not_call_the_description_fitter
   with AssertionError: sanitize_comment still depends on the description fitter: poisoning
   WikiTextCodec.fit_outbound changed the comment result to 'POISONED-DESCRIPTION-FITTER'; and
   test_fit_comment_converges_with_sanitize_comment then failed on a CONTENT mismatch between
   the send-side and differ-side bodies, which is the convergence regression this AC exists to
   prevent. 5 failed, 1 passed.
 Both mutations were reverted from the committed HEAD (git checkout HEAD -- <file>), never from
 uncommitted work.

BOUNDARY DISCIPLINE: every expected length in the new test is a MODULE-LOCAL LITERAL
 (_STOCK_CEILING = 32767, _RAISED_CEILING = 100000, _LONG_BODY_LEN = 50000, and inline 500 /
 4096), deliberately NOT imported from the code under test — an expectation derived from the
 constant under test moves with the code and can never fail. Every assertion is on the
 RESULTING BODY (its length and its content), never on "no exception raised".

GATES
 make lint PASS; make typecheck PASS (mypy, 416 source files). Module sizes, all far under the
 800-LOC cap: _config_schema.py 719 -> 725; jira_datacenter/backend.py 378 -> 441;
 jira_datacenter/settings.py 88 -> 125. scripts/gen_env_registry.py regenerated: NO diff to
 docs/env-vars.md, which is expected — that registry is derived from literal os.environ reads
 under src/rebar, and REBAR_RECONCILER_COMMENT_MAX_CHARS is auto-derived by the config layer
 rather than read as a string literal, exactly like the existing
 REBAR_RECONCILER_DELETION_PROBE_LIMIT. Local runs: the new file 6/6 green; the whole
 tests/unit/rebar_reconciler suite 1978 passed / 1 xfailed, including the DC characterization,
 richtext-port, held-out and comment-length-convergence tests that pin the old behaviour.

NOT DONE / FOLLOW-UP: docs/config.md was not updated with a row for
 [tool.rebar.reconciler].comment_max_chars — the file was outside this change's agreed file
 ownership (several agents are working in parallel). It is a one-row documentation addition and
 should be picked up by whoever owns docs/config.md next.

compiled_state.description:
# DC's comment ceiling is admin-configurable and rebar hardcodes the default

## The defect

`adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` `sanitize_comment` truncates comment bodies at
`WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` (32767), a compile-time constant. On Jira Data Center that ceiling is the
default of the admin-settable property `jira.text.field.character.limit`, whose documented range is
`0` (unlimited) to `2147483647`.

So on an instance where an administrator has RAISED the limit or set it to `0`, rebar truncates
comments that Jira would have accepted in full. **That is data loss, and it is silent to the author
of the comment** — the operator sees a truncation warning
(`jira_family/sanitizers.py:143-148`), which is why this is low-severity rather than invisible, but
the text is still gone from the remote and the local/remote bodies then differ permanently.

This is NOT the "32767 is the wrong number" defect that was originally suspected and is now refuted
(see below). It is narrower: the number is right for a STOCK instance and wrong for a CONFIGURED one.

## Established provenance (so nobody re-litigates the number)

`jira.text.field.character.limit`, from Jira's own `jpm.xml`:

    description: "The maximum number of characters to be entered for a single field.
                  Affects Description, Environment, Comments and Text custom fields.
                  0 means unlimited."
    default-value: 32767

Corroborated by JRASERVER-28519 (Resolved/Fixed, fix versions 6.4.1 / 7.0.0): "starting with JIRA
7.0 and Cloud, `jira.text.field.character.limit` will be set to 32767 by default." The DC admin page
"Configuring advanced settings" confirms the property, its field scope, `0` = unlimited and the
2147483647 maximum, but does NOT state the default.

Comments and text custom fields share ONE property and therefore one number, by design — so binding
DC's comment limit to the same constant as its description limit is structurally faithful to DC, and
must not be "fixed" by inventing a separate comment number.

Evidence the ceiling bites people in practice: JRASERVER-64351 has 86 votes from users hitting it,
which is also the population most likely to have raised the limit.

## Why the fix is not simply "read the limit"

`/rest/api/2/application-properties` plausibly exposes the key, but **whether it is readable by a
non-admin PAT is NOT established and must be tested, not assumed.** rebar authenticates as an
ordinary user on DC. If the property is admin-only, discovery is unavailable and the remedy is
configuration only.

## Proposed remediation, cheapest first

1. Make the DC comment ceiling CONFIGURABLE, defaulting to 32767. This alone closes the data-loss
   window for any operator who knows their instance's setting.
2. OPTIONALLY probe `application-properties` at connect time and log a warning when the instance's
   value disagrees with the configured one. Gate this on actually confirming the endpoint is readable
   by rebar's credential.
3. Do NOT change the default. It is correct for stock Jira >= 7.0 and matches every independent
   implementation surveyed (carrier-io/dusty annotates its own 32767 as "the
   jira.text.field.character.limit default value").

No surveyed OSS integration queries the live limit — all hardcode — so (1) brings rebar to parity
with the field and (2) would make it more correct than the field.

## Two latent traps worth fixing in the same area (not themselves data loss today)

* The constant is named `WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` and the comment at `jira_family/rich_text.py:56-60`
  attributes the number to Cloud comment limits, which REVERSES the actual causality. Renaming it
  and citing the property would stop the code asserting a false provenance.
* `sanitize_comment` reuses `fit_outbound`, the DESCRIPTION fitter. Harmless today (plain character
  truncation) but Cloud shows why the coupling is dangerous: Cloud's description fitter is
  ADF-SIZE-based (`_ADF_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT` = 32000 ADF chars, fitted empirically because
  `text_to_adf` inflates — a 32767-char description was observed serializing to ~50,566 ADF chars)
  and would be catastrophically wrong applied to comments. Any future change to the DC description
  fitter silently retargets comments.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] the DC comment ceiling is settable by configuration, defaulting to 32767, with the default's
      provenance (`jira.text.field.character.limit` + JRASERVER-28519) cited at the binding
- [ ] a comment longer than the configured ceiling but shorter than a raised one is NOT truncated
      when the ceiling is configured upward, proven by a RED-first unit test
- [ ] whether `/rest/api/2/application-properties` is readable by rebar's non-admin PAT is
      determined empirically and RECORDED; if it is not, discovery is dropped and that is stated
- [ ] `sanitize_comment` no longer depends on the description fitter, so a change to description
      fitting cannot retarget comments
- [ ] mutation-checked: reverting the configurability turns the new test red for the right reason

file_impact.reason: sanitize_comment must take a configurable ceiling instead of hardcoding WIKI_DESCRIPTION_LIMIT, and stop depending on the description fitter
carry the configurable DC comment ceiling with 32767 as the documented default
NEW: prove a comment under a raised ceiling is not truncated, and that the default stays 32767

compiled_state.title: DC comment ceiling is admin-configurable; rebar hardcodes the default
